book.title: 相思
book.subtitle: 一颗红豆，装着一份想念

poem.author: 王维
englishLines: Red beans grow in the southern land,
How many new branches come with spring?
May you gather a few of them,
For they carry the deepest remembrance.

appreciation.zh: 小小的红豆被诗人变成想念的信物，让看不见的牵挂有了颜色和形状。
appreciation.en: The poet turns tiny red beans into keepsakes, giving invisible affection a bright color and a gentle shape.

pages.zhText:
红豆生南国，
春来发几枝。
愿君多采撷，
此物最相思。
pages.enText:
Red beans grow in the southern land,
How many new branches come with spring?
May you gather a few of them,
For they carry the deepest remembrance.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Spring morning in a lush southern Tang garden, a thoughtful young poet in a pale celadon robe stands beneath a red-bean tree with fresh green leaves and a few bright red seeds, holding a small plain cloth pouch as a keepsake, warm distant hills and elegant negative space, no text in image.

pages.zhText:
红豆生南国，
温暖的南方，红豆树长得青翠又茂盛。
pages.enText:
Red beans grow in the southern land.
In the warm south, the tree grows green and full.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Wide view of the same southern garden and red-bean tree thriving beside misty blue-green hills, the same poet small beneath its canopy, several red seeds visible among glossy leaves, no text in image.

pages.zhText:
春来发几枝。
春风一吹，枝头悄悄冒出许多嫩芽。
pages.enText:
How many new branches come with spring?
The spring breeze wakes tender shoots along the branches.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Close-medium spring scene of tender new shoots opening on the same red-bean tree while the same poet gently lifts one branch to look, soft breeze moving his robe and fresh leaves, no text in image.

pages.zhText:
愿君多采撷，
诗人想把几颗红豆送给远方的朋友。
pages.enText:
May you gather a few of them.
The poet wishes a distant friend could keep a few.
pages.illustrationPrompt: The same poet carefully gathers a few fallen bright red seeds from a clean woven mat beneath the tree into the same small cloth pouch, treating them as keepsakes rather than food, calm child-friendly action, no text in image.

pages.zhText:
此物最相思。
一颗小小的红豆，像一声轻轻的‘我想你’。
pages.enText:
For they carry the deepest remembrance.
One tiny red bean can softly say, ‘I remember you.’
pages.illustrationPrompt: Gentle close view of the same poet holding one red seed safely in his open palm beside the tied cloth pouch, expression warm and thoughtful, distant migrating birds suggesting a faraway friend without a thought bubble, no text in image.

pages.zhText: 春天让树枝长出新芽，也让诗人想起远方的朋友。红豆虽小，牵挂却很长。
pages.enText: Spring grows new branches and awakens thoughts of a distant friend. The bean is small, but the bond reaches far.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Poetic wide landscape with the same poet beneath the red-bean tree in the foreground and a winding river road leading through southern mountains toward a tiny distant pavilion, the red pouch held close, one continuous real scene, no text in image.

pages.zhText: 想念不一定要说很多话。有时，一件小小的信物就能替心记住一个人。
pages.enText: Remembrance does not need many words. A tiny keepsake can help the heart hold someone close.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Quiet warm scene of the same poet tying the small pouch securely to his sash while looking toward the distant road with a soft smile, red-bean leaves framing open sky, no sadness or text in image.

pages.zhText:
红豆生南国，
春来发几枝。
愿君多采撷，
此物最相思。
再轻轻读一遍吧。
pages.enText:
Red beans grow in the southern land,
How many new branches come with spring?
May you gather a few of them,
For they carry the deepest remembrance.
Now read it softly once more.
pages.illustrationPrompt: Closing spring sunset in the same garden, the poet walks along a path with the keepsake pouch as the red-bean tree glows against misty southern hills, a few red seeds and new green leaves forming a gentle visual rhythm, no text in image.
